description:
fz-k22.26 separates BackendDirectCallableEntry (direct target/capture/ABI authority) from BackendCallableEntry (actual transport publication). The split fixes direct-only backend inventory and fallback transport binding, but full native tests prove NativeLowerer still eagerly constructs boundaries from every direct entry.

Goal
Native closure boundaries are materialized only at a concrete closure-producing use: published values use their publication association; direct-only closures derive a local boundary from the exact concrete producer/call target. The direct registry remains lookup authority, never a global closure-value inventory.

Signal
Full cargo test --lib after the split fails typed-capture/direct-target telemetry, multi-target capture surface, source-lambda JIT, published target flow, and direct-only inventory contracts. Treating all direct entries as native boundaries collapses direct executable authority into first-class value authority.

Strategy
Trace concrete FunctionRef/Lambda construction and direct call lowering to identify the authoritative target at that use. Encode the boundary derivation there, retaining publication boundary data only for actual transport values. Do not restore None-boundary publication records or synthesize boundaries globally from the direct registry.

Acceptance
The full native contract/JIT regressions pass with direct-only entries absent from published inventory and no duplicate target/capture/ABI authority.
title: Derive native direct boundaries at concrete closure producers
